title: The Gospel and Atonement
short_answer: Jesus died as a substitute for sinners so that those who trust in Him may be forgiven and reconciled to God.
explanation: The Gospel is the good news that Jesus Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, was buried, and rose again the third day. His death was substitutionary — He bore the penalty sinners deserved.
logical_reasoning: God is just and must punish sin. Yet God is love and desires to save. The cross satisfies both justice and mercy: sin is punished in Christ, and sinners are forgiven through faith.
defense_response: The atonement is not symbolic. Scripture teaches substitution (Isaiah 53:5), propitiation (Romans 3:25), and imputation (2 Corinthians 5:21).
